source.build: cargo build --locked --release; binaries identified by SHA-256
source.harness: launch-video/showreel/capture/harness.patch applied to dev/ for screen size, GDK scale and the binaries bind only; no app source changed

where: dev/verify.sh session: private Xvfb 3840x2160 at GDK scale 2 (Qt scale 2, Firefox devPixelsPerPx 2), Openbox without decorations, private HOME, D-Bus, AT-SPI bus, PID and network namespaces (loopback only)
real: The production mluva binary: F9 through its global-shortcut path (toggle-recording-f9), capture, the compatible provider's 3 s batch previews and final upload, History, target capture at Start and delivery at Stop

The production Omarchy widget (linux/quickshell/mluva.dictation with Omarchy's own Commons and Ui modules) in Quickshell, fed by the real mluva-shell bridge: recording light, timer, 'Waiting for speech…', live words, then hidden on Stop

Delivery: Mluva captured Firefox's focused 'Your reply' field over AT-SPI at Start, revalidated it at Stop and sent its guarded keyboard paste (xdotool ctrl+v, the X11 helper Mluva chooses); History records delivery_outcome 'pasted'
scripted: F9 presses: the shortcut portal is the repository's fixture peer; Activated/Deactivated signals for toggle-recording-f9
Microphone: the repository's PCM fixture (quiet synthetic audio, real-time pace)
Words: launch-video/launch/capture/speech_field.py returns the words whose scripted time falls in each 3 s preview chunk, and the whole sentence for the final upload
The page: launch-video/launch/capture/fixtures/notes.html (invented notes; Firefox chrome hidden with userChrome.css)
Two clicks with xdotool on the private display before recording (the page, then the field), so the field's focus event reaches Mluva after Firefox's accessibility tree is live
org.a11y.Bus on the session bus: launch-video/launch/capture/a11y_status.py stands in for at-spi-bus-launcher's front, as rust/mluva-gtk/examples/firefox_text_peer.rs does

visible.recording_widget_frames: 151-721 (light, timer, live words; three word chunks)

notes: Live words arrive in three 3 s chunks: the compatible provider's batch preview at its shortest chunk. ElevenLabs Scribe realtime streams word by word; it was not used.

X11 has no compositor here, so the widget's translucent surface is not blended with the page. The page background is pure black (#000), over which a blended and an unblended surface give the same pixels.
The text arrives by Mluva's keyboard paste, not direct insertion: Mluva deliberately pastes into Firefox fields.
